title: Soler: what people used to do

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *soler* from B1 Unit 5. *Soler* + infinitive says that something happens or happened regularly. To talk about everyday life in the past you use the imperfect: *solía comer*, *solían cultivar*. It is a good way to describe habits in a world that no longer exists.

items.spanish: Los campesinos solían cultivar maíz, frijol y calabaza.
items.english: The farmers used to grow maize, beans and squash.

items.spanish: En los Andes la gente solía comer papa y quinua.
items.english: In the Andes people used to eat potatoes and quinoa.

items.spanish: La gente solía tomar una bebida amarga de cacao.
items.english: People used to drink a bitter cacao drink.

items.spanish: Los jugadores solían usar una pelota de caucho.
items.english: The players used to use a rubber ball.

sections.content: *Solía* goes with *yo*, *él*, *ella*; *solían* with *ellos*, *ellas*, *ustedes*. The verb after it is always an infinitive. Do not use *soler* in the preterite for a single event: it describes habits, not one-time actions.
